      Group  continuing  core  results                                            
      Nutun assesses its performance using core continuing earnings, an alternative non-IFRS profit measure, alongside IFRS
      profit. Non-IFRS measures are not uniformly defined nor used by all entities and may not be comparable with similarly labelled
      measures and disclosures provided by other entities. Management considers that core continuing earnings is an appropriate
      alternative performance measure to enhance the comparability and understanding of the financial performance of the group.
      The group has set out its policy to calculate core continuing earnings below.
      Nutun calculates headline earnings in accordance with the latest SAICA Circular 1/2023 ‘Headline Earnings’.
      Core continuing earnings is calculated by adjusting headline earnings for the following:
      • Once-off transaction costs which are directly attributable to corporate activity (primarily legal and consulting fees).
      • Adjustments on put and call options over non-controlling interests, namely imputed interest on the put option liability,
        re-measurements of the put option liability and fair value adjustments on the call option derivative.
      • Once-off or accelerated items, where these are reasonably expected not to re-occur in the ordinary course of business
        in future reporting periods.                                              
      • Adding back specified headline earnings exclusions, if the gain/loss is considered part of Nutun’s normal operations.
      These adjustments are considered annually based on the transforming nature of the group. Management is responsible for
      the calculation of core continuing earnings and determining the inclusions and exclusions in accordance with the policy.

      6.1  Credit risk                                                            
           Credit risk is the risk of loss arising from the failure of a client or counterparty to discharge an obligation to the
           group. The primary credit risks that the group are exposed to as at 31 March 2026 relate to the risks associated with
           the purchased book debts, if the books fail to perform in accordance with estimate net future cash flows. Trade
           receivables include receivables from clients that have standard 30-day terms. The clients are diversified across
           numerous industries and geographies and do not result in significant concentration risk. It is not the group’s strategy
           to avoid credit risk, but rather to manage credit risk within the group’s risk appetite and to earn an appropriate
           risk-adjusted return.                                                  
           The group limits its counterparty exposure arising from money market instruments by dealing only with well
           established financial institutions of high credit standing. Deposits are limited to the big five banks within South
           Africa.                                                                
           Credit risk management and measurement                                 
           Each subsidiary is responsible for the identification, measurement, management, control and reporting of credit
           risk within their business units. Exposure to credit losses is managed by collectability of purchased book debts.
           Impairments are monitored and provided for using statistical techniques including experiential and behavioural
           models. These models are based on customers’ financial performance information while on book and assume that
           recent performance is a strong indicator of future performance. In the case of key asset classes, independent models
           are developed to monitor the robustness of the primary models relative to actual performance and to optimise their
           effectiveness. Models are either developed internally or by expert external advisors.
           The group assumes that the credit risk on a financial instrument has not increased significantly if the financial
           instrument is determined to have a low credit risk at the reporting date.
           Measurement of expected credit losses (ECL)                            
           The group measures ECL of a financial instrument in a way that reflects:
           • An unbiased and probability-weighted amount that is determined by evaluating a range of possible outcomes;
           • The time value of money; and                                         
           • Reasonable and supportable information that is available without undue cost or effort at the reporting date about
             past events, current conditions and forecasts of future economic conditions.
           The maximum period considered when measuring ECL is the maximum contractual period (including extension
           options) over which the group is exposed to credit risk, and not a longer period, even if that period is consistent
           with business practice.                                                
           The measurement of ECL is a function of the probability of default (PD), loss given default (LGD) and exposure
           at default (EAD). The assessment of the probability of default and loss given write-offs is based on historical data
           adjusted by forward-looking information as described above.            
           As for the EAD for financial assets, this is represented by the assets’ gross carrying amount at the reporting date
           and other relevant forward-looking information.                        
           For financial assets, the ECL is estimated as the difference between all contractual cash flows that are due to the
           group in accordance with the contract and all the cash flows that the group expects to receive, discounted at
           the original effective interest rate.

           Purchased book debts                                                   
           Investment process                                                     
           Prior to the acquisition of purchased book debts (PBDs), there is a defined investment process that is followed in
           accordance with guidelines determined by a constituted investment committee. PBDs are acquired from various
           credit providers in multiple sectors. Valuations are determined by projecting the present value of anticipated monthly
           collections, net of directly attributable collection costs, using past performance characteristics applicable to similar
           PBDs. Said valuations are ultimately presented to the investment committee to decide upon pricing and bidding
           strategy.                                                              
           Collections process                                                    
           The Insights, Data & Enterprise Analytics (IDEA) team continually develops and recalibrates insights and analytics
           used by operations to optimise the collection processes, and infrastructure, associated with non-performing debt
           collected.                                                             
           Method of provisioning and fair valuing                                
           PBDs are classified as purchased credit-impaired (POCI) financial assets (stage 3) on initial recognition based on the
           presumption that events that have a detrimental impact on the estimated future cash flows of these financial assets
           have occurred before acquisition and initial recognition. The classification of PBDs does not change subsequent
           to initial recognition, even in the unlikely event of the expected cash flows associated thereto returning to full
           contractual terms.                                                     
           Any changes in lifetime expected credit losses (ECLs) are recognised in profit or loss. The group recognises
           favourable changes in lifetime ECLs as an impairment gain, even if lifetime ECLs are less than the amount of ECLs
           that were included in the estimated cash flows on initial recognition. 
           Nutun utilises statistical techniques and models to value PBDs on a monthly basis. Each PBD is modelled based on
           the collection activity applied to it. A combination of inflows applicable to each PBD and the direct, activity-based,
           cost projections applicable thereto are used to determine a net cash flow over a rolling 12-month period, which is
           subsequently discounted to present value using a credit-adjusted effective interest rate to determine its amortised
           cost value. The weighted average credit-adjusted effective interest rate at period end is 19.2% (31 March 2025: 17.9%;
           30 September 2025: 18.4%).                                             
           Other financial assets, recognised within the purchase book debts, include a receivables balance measured at fair
           value. The valuation technique applicable thereto calculates the present value of all future cash flows associated
           thereto net of all associated costs.                                   
           Carrying value of purchased book debts                                 
           The Nutun South Africa business model continues to gain relevance as slow economic growth drive up indebtedness
           and impair consumers’ ability to service their debt, leaving consumer facing entities with significantly larger
           non-performing loans (NPL) portfolios to manage. These impairment model parameters have been applied in
           determining expected cash shortfalls arising from non-payment in the best estimate provision on the loan book as
           at 31 March 2026. These books are not subsequently managed based on the credit risk rating but rather on a cash

      6.3  Fair value disclosure                                                  
           Fair values of financial instruments carried at amortised cost         
           The fair value of a financial instrument is the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability
           between market participants at the measurement date.                   
           The best evidence of the fair value of a financial instrument at initial recognition is the transaction price (i.e. the fair
           value of the consideration given or received) unless the fair value of that instrument is evidenced by comparison with
           other observable current market transactions in the same instrument (i.e. without modification or repackaging) or
           based on a valuation technique whose variables include only data from observable markets.
           The method of determining the fair value of financial instruments is analysed into the following categories:
           Level 1 Unadjusted quoted prices in active markets where the quoted price is readily available and the price
                represents actual and regularly occurring market transactions on an arm’s length basis.
           Level 2 Valuation techniques using market observable inputs, including:
                • Using recent arm’s length market transactions;                  
                • Reference to the current fair value of similar instruments; and 
                • Discounted cash flow analysis, pricing models or other techniques commonly used by market
                  participants                                                    
           Level 3 Valuation techniques, as described for level 2 above, for which not all inputs are market observable prices
                or rates. Such a financial instrument is initially recognised at the transaction price, which is the best
                indicator of fair value, although the value obtained from the relevant valuation model may differ. The
                difference between the transaction price and the model value, commonly referred to as “day one profit
                or loss’, is either amortised over the life of the transaction, deferred until the instrument’s fair value can
                be determined using market observable inputs, or realised through settlement.
           The valuation techniques in level 2 and level 3 use inputs such as interest rate yield curves, equity prices and currency
           prices/yields, volatilities, and the correlation between inputs. The models used in these valuation techniques are
           calibrated against industry standards, economic models and against transaction process, where applicable.
           Valuation methods and assumptions:                                     
           Principal book portfolios are held at amortised cost. The balance at the end of the period is calculated based on
           the expected future cash flows which are adjusted for risk as it takes historical cash flows into account to predict

### 1. Executive Investment Thesis & 12-Month JSE Price Target

**Core thesis — SELL, R0.55 target (-38.2%).** Nutun is not a growth story; it is a **covenant-sensitive, going-concern-adjacent consumer debt purchaser** whose headline "EBITDA +28.5% to R790m" is a **CODM-view artefact** that adds back the R597m PBD amortisation representing the economic cost of the book. The statutory reality is a **continuing loss of R63m** (LPS −8.1c), **negative operating cash flow of R(111)m**, and a **R901m gap** between "Core EBITDA" and actual operating cash. Equity fell to **R1,329m** (from R1,396m), the entire **R3,845m PBD book is pledged**, and the verified undrawn liquidity of **R475m** sits against a **R1,396m 12-month maturity wall** — a **R809m near-term funding gap**.

**Structural headwinds (dominant):**
1. **ECL coverage collapse** — total coverage fell from 20.4% (Mar-25) to **12.6%** (Mar-26); the largest segment (Banking-unsecured, 69% of book) fell to **9.6%** from 19.4%, with a **R241m impairment loss** booked on that segment. 2. **12-month ECL horizon on lifetime POCI assets** — structurally understates the allowance given the multi-year collection tail implied by ERC R8,366m vs carrying R4,489m (1.86x).
3. **Thin risk-adjusted spread** — CAEIR 19.2% less CLR ~8.5% less funding ~9.1% = **~2.0% net spread**; a 200bps CLR deterioration wipes it out.
4. **100% floating-rate, fully-secured, short-dated debt** — no fixed-rate hedge; FV swing of R365m in six months; no unencumbered collateral to raise new secured funding.
5. **72% revenue concentration in UK+US** (FX-exposed); SA only 22.4%; SA segment is **PBT-negative at R(123)m**.
6. **Unaudited/unreviewed H1 2026** — restatement risk on PBD carrying value, amortisation and CAEIR.
7. **Dividend suspended** since FY2023; no resumption forecast.

**Structural tailwinds (insufficient to offset):**
- Repo rate cuts reduce floating funding cost (management cites R203m SA net interest, −7%).
- Agentic AI rollout in collections could improve efficiency over the medium term.
- International BPO billable seats +20% to 2,491; client base 36.
- New PBD acquisitions at "healthy returns" (R382m in H1) — but these dilute aggregate ECL coverage and mask legacy deterioration.

**Verdict:** The market price of R0.89 already discounts distress (treasury shares bought at R1 vs ~R6.90 book). guardrails.title: Forecast Cash and Financing Must Reconcile
guardrails.rule_text: For every forecast period, reconcile opening cash plus operating, investing and financing cash flows and separately identified FX or scope changes to closing cash on the forecast balance sheet. Reconcile new borrowing, repayments and equity issuance to debt balances, equity and dilution. State the cash definition and rounding tolerance; bridge restricted cash, held-for-sale cash and overdrafts included in cash equivalents explicitly, without double counting. An unresolved material residual invalidates the forecast and dependent valuation; missing inputs are NOT VERIFIED, never PASS. Example: opening 100 + operating 20 - capex 10 + financing 5 = closing 115 passes; opening 100 plus net change -815 cannot produce closing 95 without an explicit 810 reconciling inflow.

guardrails.title: Statutory Operating Cash Flow to FCFF/FCFE Bridge & Capex/Lease Deduction
guardrails.rule_text: Prohibits labeling statutory Cash Generated from Operations (before capex, lease principal repayments, and interest) as Free Cash Flow to Equity (FCFE) or Free Cash Flow to Firm (FCFF). Models must explicitly bridge operating cash flow to true free cash flow by deducting replacement and expansion capex, IFRS 16 lease principal repayments, net finance costs, and working capital normalizations.

guardrails.title: Cross-Section HEPS, Multiple & Target Price Identity
guardrails.rule_text: Compute your Section 3 (P&L and HEPS) and Section 4 (DCF and P/E / EV/EBITDA valuation) numbers BEFORE writing the Section 1 Executive Summary Card commentary. The 12-Month Target Price, Reference Price, Forecast HEPS (e.g. FY27E HEPS in R or cents), and Target P/E or EV/EBITDA multiple cited in the Section 1 Executive Summary Card 'Basis & Key Commentary' cell MUST be 100% identical to Section 3 and Section 4 (never cite one HEPS/multiple in Section 1 commentary and a different HEPS/multiple in Section 4).

guardrails.title: DCF Schedule Reproducibility & Anti-Handwaving Component Bridge
guardrails.rule_text: Mandates explicit disclosure of annual forecast FCFF/FCFE, terminal value, WACC/discount rate, and a step-by-step numerical EV-to-Equity bridge. Forbids applying qualitative, unmodeled percentage uplifts to blended valuation components; any adjustment between underlying component valuations (e.g. DCF and P/E) and the published target price must be modeled directly within the underlying cash flows or valuation multiples.

guardrails.title: Full Legal Entity Name Verification Across Notes (No Acronym Conflation)
guardrails.rule_text: Never abbreviate two distinct legal entities to the same acronym and claim an accounting classification contradiction. When evaluating entities with similar names, acronyms, or operating divisions, always compare and cross-check full legal entity names across notes before concluding on whether an entity is a joint venture, joint operation, associate, or subsidiary.

guardrails.title: Ordinary Shareholder NAV versus Contributed Capital
guardrails.rule_text: Calculate statutory ordinary book value/NAV per share from equity attributable to parent ordinary shareholders, excluding non-controlling interests and preference or other non-ordinary claims, divided by ordinary shares outstanding net of treasury shares at the same measurement date. Reconcile retained earnings or accumulated losses and reserves; never label contributed share capital alone as NAV. Use date-matched closing shares rather than silently substituting an earnings weighted-average denominator. Adjusted or tangible NAV is permitted only when clearly labelled and reconciled to statutory ordinary equity, with every adjustment disclosed. NAV is not automatically market fair value. Example: parent ordinary equity 1,329 million / 780.651033 million net shares = approximately 1.70 ZAR/share; share capital 5,410 million / those shares is not book NAV.

guardrails.title: Mandatory Historical Actuals Base Column & Currency Unit Consistency
guardrails.rule_text: In Section 2 (Operational Forecast) and Section 3 (Income Statement & Cash Flow Bridge), always include the reported historical base period column(s) (e.g. FY25A and/or 1H26A) alongside FY26E, FY27E, and FY28E so annualized run-rates, operating expenses, and margins are anchored to audited actuals. Never label a ZAR-converted segment revenue row as EUR'm or USD'm; ensure every row's currency unit label matches the numbers in that row.

guardrails.title: IFRS 16 EV-to-Equity & Cash Flow Consistency
guardrails.rule_text: Never mix Pre-IFRS 16 cash flows/EBITDA with Post-IFRS 16 lease debt in an Enterprise Value (EV) to Equity bridge. If EV is derived by discounting or applying a multiple to Pre-IFRS 16 EBITDA/FCFF (where cash lease rental payments are already deducted as an operating outflow), DO NOT subtract capitalised IFRS 16 lease liabilities again in the EV-to-Equity bridge (and do not subtract lease principal payments a second time in FCFE). Conversely, if subtracting net IFRS 16 lease liabilities in the EV bridge, you must discount Post-IFRS 16 EBITDA/FCFF before lease payments. Always state explicitly whether your valuation bridge is on a Pre-IFRS 16 or Post-IFRS 16 basis.

guardrails.title: Withhold Valuation Until Material Dependencies Are Resolved
guardrails.rule_text: If a material cash-flow, forecast, financing, share-count, portfolio or valuation dependency fails reconciliation or remains unsupported, return VALUATION WITHHELD - MATERIAL ISSUES UNRESOLVED. Preserve verified historical analysis and risks, identify each blocker and the evidence or correction needed, and carry unresolved Stage 1 findings forward. Do not publish a target, rating bands, upside, dividend yield, TSR or investment recommendation; use JSON null, never zero or HOLD. Illustrative scenarios must remain clearly conditional and separate from the headline valuation. READY requires explicit source evidence, consistent periods and scopes, cash/debt/portfolio roll-forwards, equity financing and terminal-policy consistency, valuation-bridge and sensitivity checks. Assumptions may be used when supported and disclosed; they cannot conceal material missing inputs. Application checks of declared evidence and numeric reconciliations do not replace independent review.

guardrails.title: Forecast PAT-to-HEPS Reconciliation & Net Finance Sign Integrity
guardrails.rule_text: Forecast HEPS (cents) MUST equal (Forecast Headline Earnings in R'm / Weighted-Average Shares in millions * 100) and move directionally with Forecast PAT unless explicit non-headline items (e.g. PPE/investment property fair-value gains or goodwill impairments) are itemized in the bridge. Never forecast a sharp drop in PAT alongside an unexplained rise in HEPS. Also verify whether historical Net Finance is net finance income (+, e.g. when JV finance income exceeds P&L finance cost after interest capitalisation) or net finance expense (-), and preserve the exact sign so the P&L sums vertically.

guardrails.title: Statutory vs. Normalized P&L Vertical Arithmetic & Impairment Bridge
guardrails.rule_text: Every income statement table must sum vertically line-by-line (Revenue - Cost of sales = Gross profit; Gross profit + Other revenue/income - Net operating expenses = Operating profit). Always verify from the primary AFS notes whether statutory Operating Profit is already stated AFTER impairments, restructuring, or extraordinary items before subtracting them; never subtract Note 7/exceptional impairments a second time from a statutory Operating Profit that already includes them, and ensure historical continuing PAT and HEPS match the statutory AFS reconciliation identically.

guardrails.title: Strictly Ascending ZAR Rating Bands
guardrails.rule_text: In the opening JSON block and Section 1 table, rating_bands thresholds MUST be strictly ascending in ZAR per share: strong_buy_max_zar < buy_max_zar < hold_max_zar < sell_max_zar == strong_sell_above_zar, anchored around target_price_zar (Strong Buy <= Target/1.30, Buy <= Target/1.15, Hold <= Target/0.95, Sell <= Target/0.85, Strong Sell > Target/0.85). Never output identical ZAR values for Hold and Sell thresholds.

guardrails.title: Sensitivity Cells Must Reproduce the Valuation
guardrails.rule_text: Recalculate every sensitivity cell using the same documented base valuation formula, changing only the named inputs. The central case MUST reproduce the published base target within a declared rounding tolerance. Preserve debt, share count, cash-flow basis, valuation bridges and all discounts unless explicitly varied. Show the formula and full transformation for any additional haircut; unexplained cells invalidate the sensitivity conclusions. Nonlinear models are allowed when their actual formulas are used; do not impose constant derivatives from another method. Missing formulas or inputs are NOT VERIFIED. Example: with 3,845 million of PBD assets, a 0.05 multiple change and one 25% discount over 780.7 million shares imply a 0.18469 ZAR/share change; 0.07 without a disclosed transformation fails. This supplements SOTP arithmetic and prohibits double counting adjustments.

guardrails.title: Verified Weighted-Average Share Count & Continuing HEPS Denominator
guardrails.rule_text: Always extract and state the exact basic and diluted weighted-average number of ordinary shares (in millions, net of treasury shares) from the AFS EPS/HEPS note. Never confuse Headline Earnings in R'm with the share count in millions. In Stage 2 Section 3, include an explicit 'Weighted-Average Shares (m)' row immediately above 'Continuing HEPS (cents)', divide Continuing Headline Earnings (excluding discontinued operations and capital/Note 7 items) by that exact share count, and verify that full-year forecast HEPS is consistent with H1 continuing HEPS already banked.

guardrails.title: Strict SOTP Vertical Arithmetic & Prohibition of DCF + Working Capital Double-Counting
guardrails.rule_text: In Section 4 SOTP / DCF valuation tables, every component row MUST sum vertically to Total Enterprise Value (TEV), Equity Value (TEV less Net Debt), SOTP Fair Value per Share (Equity Value / Net Shares), and Target Price (ZAR). If a percentage risk/liquidity discount is applied (e.g. 25% discount), the discount ZAR per share and resulting Target Price MUST equal SOTP Fair Value per Share * (1 - discount%); never switch denominators mid-table. Never add book working capital (Inventory, Contract Assets/WIP) or Goodwill on top of a segment DCF/NPV that already discounts the cash flows generated by those operating assets.

guardrails.title: Gross vs. Net Treasury Share Count & Parent vs. Consolidated Dividend Reconciliation
guardrails.rule_text: Before flagging an arithmetic discrepancy between parent-company dividends paid/declared and net shares in issue, always check gross issued shares vs treasury shares held by subsidiaries or share trusts (e.g. in the Integrated Report dividend declaration or Stated Capital note). Under South African corporate law, the parent company pays the gross dividend on all gross issued shares, whereas the Consolidated Statement of Changes in Equity and Cash Flow Statement eliminate intra-group dividends paid on treasury shares.

guardrails.title: Construction POC Revenue Recognition, Retentions & Joint Operations
guardrails.rule_text: Cross-check IFRS 15 percentage-of-completion (POC) revenue against contract assets (unbilled WIP), retentions receivable aging, customer advances (contract liabilities), and proportionate consolidation of joint operations vs equity-accounted JVs.

guardrails.title: Consumer Lending IFRS 9 Stage Migration & Purchased Book Debt (PBD) Amortization
guardrails.rule_text: Reconcile gross loan book and Purchased Book Debt (PBD) carrying values against Estimated Remaining Collections (ERC), separating cash collections applied to revenue yield vs principal amortization and Stage 1/2/3 ECL coverage.

guardrails.title: Purchased Book Debt (PBD) Amortisation Exclusion from Operating Cash Flow
guardrails.rule_text: When valuing consumer debt purchasers and collectors, models are strictly prohibited from treating PBD amortisation as a non-cash add-back in Free Cash Flow to Equity (FCFE). Because portfolio replenishments (PBD acquisitions) are required to sustain collections, models must reflect net cash collections after portfolio acquisition reinvestment.

guardrails.title: POCI Cumulative Gains, Loss Allowances and Portfolio Scope
guardrails.rule_text: For purchased or originated credit-impaired (POCI) principal portfolios, identify the acquisition baseline and reconcile gross carrying amount, signed cumulative changes in lifetime expected credit losses, and net carrying amount using the original notes. A favourable cumulative impairment gain is NOT a conventional loss-coverage reserve: do not divide it by gross carrying amount and call the result loss coverage or describe its decline as a coverage collapse. Preserve reported labels such as ECL allowance while explaining their economic sign. Reconcile opening balance, gains or losses on new and historical portfolios, and closing balance. Separate amortised-cost POCI principal portfolios from other purchased-book-debt assets measured at FVTPL; do not apply one ECL regime to both. Example: gross 3,414 plus cumulative gain 431 = net 3,845; 431/3,414 is not conventional loss coverage. A rolling 12-month modelling disclosure warrants a lifetime/tail-methodology check, not an unsupported conclusion about the amount or direction of misstatement. Missing methodology is NOT VERIFIED.

guardrails.title: Banking Risk-Adjusted NIM, Credit Loss Ratio (CLR) & CET1 Capital Bridge
guardrails.rule_text: Evaluate Net Interest Margin (NIM) net of the Credit Loss Ratio (CLR bps) across Stage 1/2/3 loan portfolios, and verify dividend payout capacity against Basel III CET1 regulatory capital buffers and Return on Equity (ROE) vs Cost of Equity (Ke).

guardrails.title: IT Services Recurring ARR vs. Unbilled Contract Asset (WIP) Cash Conversion
guardrails.rule_text: Separate high-multiple recurring managed services/ARR from low-margin hardware/software resale, and audit whether EBITDA growth is backed by cash collection or trapped in unbilled IFRS 15 contract assets (WIP).

guardrails.title: IT Services Hardware Reselling vs. Core Software/Services Margin Disaggregation
guardrails.rule_text: When analyzing IT and software services companies, models must strictly disaggregate low-margin OEM hardware pass-through revenue from high-margin recurring services and own IP software licenses. The model is prohibited from using consolidated EV/Sales or applying software multiples to hardware revenue, and must explicitly account for the negative working capital drag of hardware supplier payables.

guardrails.title: Mining By-Product Subsidized AISC vs. Standalone Starter Phase Costs
guardrails.rule_text: For multi-commodity deposits or phased mine developments, the model is strictly prohibited from applying consolidated Life-of-Mine (LOM) headline AISC (subsidized by co-product or by-product zinc/silver/PGM credits) to standalone single-commodity starter pits or trial mining phases. Standalone cash costs and sustaining capex must be independently modeled.

guardrails.title: Mining Inferred Mineral Resource Haircut in LOM Production Schedules
guardrails.rule_text: Any portion of a Life-of-Mine (LOM) production schedule or discounted cash flow model derived from Inferred Mineral Resources rather than JORC/SAMREC Audited Probable Reserves cannot be valued at par. The model must apply an explicit 25% to 50% risk discount or resource conversion delay to unproven tonnage.

guardrails.title: SA Mining Section 36 Capital Allowance & Sustaining vs. Growth Capex Split
guardrails.rule_text: Separate sustaining capital (included in AISC) from expansionary/growth project capital (excluded from AISC), and apply 100% upfront Section 36 capital redemption shields before modeling cash tax step-ups under the South African Gold Mining Tax Formula or corporate tax rate.

guardrails.title: SA REIT BPR Distributable Income & Look-Through LTV Reconciliation
guardrails.rule_text: Strip non-cash fair value property revaluations, straight-line rental accruals, and derivative mark-to-market movements from IFRS profit to arrive at SA REIT Funds From Operations (FFO) / Distributable Income per Share (DIPS), and reconcile nominal balance sheet LTV against look-through LTV including JV/associate debt.

guardrails.title: REIT Debt Paydown vs. Interest Rate Swap Over-Hedging Liability
guardrails.rule_text: When forecasting debt reduction from disposal proceeds or rights offers, the model must reconcile forecast gross borrowings against active fixed-to-floating interest rate swap notionals. If debt falls below swap notional (hedging ratio > 100%), the model must penalize earnings for over-hedged negative carry and recognize mark-to-market break-fee liabilities.

guardrails.title: REIT Yield-Stripping Asset Disposals vs. ICR Covenant Default
guardrails.rule_text: When evaluating property asset sales to reduce debt, the model must explicitly calculate whether interest expense savings exceed lost Net Property Income (NPI). If the disposed asset is an unencumbered high-yielding cash cow, the model must verify pro-forma Interest Cover Ratio (ICR) and flag covenant breach risk, even if headline Loan-to-Value (LTV) appears to improve.

guardrails.title: Retail APM Merchandise Margin vs. Total Statutory Operating Margin
guardrails.rule_text: The model must strictly distinguish non-standard Alternative Performance Measures (APMs) that calculate operating margins by dividing group EBIT solely by merchandise sales from true statutory operating margins on total revenue (including credit finance and insurance income). Models must disclose both and base consolidated operational forecasts on statutory total revenue.

guardrails.title: Retail & Trade Receivable ECL Non-Cash Movement vs. Balance Sheet Allowance Bridge
guardrails.rule_text: When auditing trade/retailer receivables and loan allowances, reconcile the Cash Flow Statement non-cash ECL movement against the Balance Sheet allowance movement by accounting for final write-offs against the allowance and fair-value discounting, and verify whether elevated credit loss run-rates persist in post-balance-sheet SENS updates.

guardrails.title: Retail Customer Credit Hidden Arrears inside Satisfactory Paid Accounts
guardrails.rule_text: When auditing credit-granting retailers, the model must not rely on reported 'Satisfactory Paid' percentage claims without probing whether overdue instalments are concealed within performing categories. The true contractual delinquency and non-performing debt ratio must be explicitly quantified in working capital and impairment assumptions.

guardrails.title: Retail Head-Lease Liability vs. Back-to-Back Franchisee Lease Receivable Netting
guardrails.rule_text: For wholesale/franchise retailers that sign head-leases on properties and sub-lease them back-to-back to independent retailers, always net the IFRS 16 finance lease receivables (Current + Non-current) against gross IFRS 16 lease liabilities to isolate the group's true net store/DC lease exposure, and distinguish Pre-IFRS 16 covenant EBITDA from Post-IFRS 16 statutory EBITDA.

guardrails.title: Working Capital Payable Stretch & Cash Conversion Normalization
guardrails.rule_text: Forbids treating operating cash flow spikes as sustainable free cash flow when driven predominantly by elongation of trade creditor days (>15% YoY increase in trade payables) or inventory freezes during network store expansion. Analysts must normalize working capital swings to multi-year historical averages and isolate supplier rebate/allowance reclassifications from core merchandise gross margins.

guardrails.title: Telco Clean Operational FCF vs. Non-Recurring Dividend Payout Cover
guardrails.rule_text: When forecasting telco dividend sustainability against free cash flow payout policies (e.g. 40-60% of FCF), strip all non-operating cash inflows such as cell-captive insurance dividends, contract-asset factoring receipts, and disposal gains. Compute dividend cover strictly against recurring, clean operational FCF post-lease principal and interest.

guardrails.title: Telco Goodwill Impairment Avoidance & Discount Rate Sensitivity Test
guardrails.rule_text: When evaluating telco CGUs in structural revenue decline (e.g. legacy IT/converged comms), never accept a 'no impairment' determination that is achieved solely by reducing the pre-tax discount rate by >200 bps without an underlying reduction in cost of capital or risk profile. Always perform a counterfactual sensitivity test holding the prior year's discount rate constant and reflect implied goodwill impairments in adjusted equity value.

guardrails.title: Telco Tower Lease Capitalisation (IFRS 16) & Spectrum/Network Capex Free Cash Flow
guardrails.rule_text: Treat recurring tower lease principal & interest payments as ongoing cash outflows when computing Free Cash Flow to Equity (FCFE), and separate one-off spectrum auction outlays from recurring network modernization capex.
